charges.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Secret
charges.description: JWT signing secret is stored directly in source code on line 6. Any collaborator, build log, or public commit exposes the secret and allows arbitrary token forging.

charges.title: Plaintext Password Verification
charges.description: User passwords are checked on line 12 via direct equality comparison without cryptographic salt or hashing (e.g., bcrypt/argon2), violating basic storage standards.

charges.title: Unbounded Token Expiration Window
charges.description: The JWT generated on line 14 omits an 'expiresIn' configuration, issuing eternal tokens that cannot be invalidated if stolen.

charges.title: Unhandled Async Rejections & User Enumeration
charges.description: The route handler lacks a try/catch boundary, risking process-level crashes on database hiccups. Line 19 confirms username existence, aiding enumeration attacks.

debate.speaker: prosecutor
debate.text: Your Honor! The defendant has committed high treason against the First Law of Security: line 6 harbors a raw cryptographic signing key in plaintext source code!

debate.speaker: defense
debate.text: A brief objection on procedural grounds! This repository was created as an internal MVP stub to unblock client frontend integration tests.

debate.speaker: prosecutor
debate.text: Internal MVP? Tell that to the users whose passwords are verified on line 12 with direct string comparison! A single data leak exposes every credential in plain daylight.

debate.speaker: defense
debate.text: We acknowledge the severity of the charges, Your Honor. The defense is prepared to introduce bcrypt hashing and move the signing key to environment configuration immediately.

debate.speaker: judge
debate.text: Good intentions do not nullify the breach radius. Eternal tokens and hardcoded keys warrant severe scrutiny under this court.

verdict.summary: The Court finds the defendant GUILTY on multiple counts of cryptographic negligence and insecure credential handling. Hardcoded keys and plaintext authentication cannot be excused by prototype deadlines.
sentence: Extract JWT_SECRET into process.env.JWT_SECRET and require it at application boot.
Migrate user passwords to salted bcrypt hashes with cost factor 12.
Enforce an explicit token lifespan (e.g., '15m') and configure standard audience/issuer headers.
Wrap async database calls with try/catch and delegate unexpected errors to express error middleware.

cannedObjections.trigger: This is only an MVP created for local testing!
cannedObjections.reply: The Court grants no immunity to 'temporary prototypes'. Hardcoded keys committed to git history survive indefinitely.

cannedObjections.trigger: Our reverse proxy sanitizes errors and terminates TLS before hitting Express!
cannedObjections.reply: Defense-in-depth is mandatory. Upstream proxies do not prevent session forging once the signing secret is leaked.

cannedObjections.trigger: We can wrap the handler in an express async error boundary!
cannedObjections.reply: A valid architectural point. Async boundaries stabilize server health, though the security charges remain fully culpable.

improvements: Extracted JWT secrets to process.env with runtime presence validation
Constrained token validity to a 15-minute expiration window
Standardized generic 401 response preventing account enumeration
Structured async error delegation via express next(err)
